chunks: Humayd ibn al-Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, from more than one, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does anything prevent you from the Salat (prayer) for the funeral corpses during these hours? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الْجَنَائِزِ: the funeral prayer (prayer for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: Does the Imam avoid funeral prayer during specific hours of the day?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) did not abstain from the funeral prayer during the four specific times of slight dislike (karahat) for general prayers, establishing that the general temporal restrictions do not apply to Salat al-Janazah. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of the funeral prayer as a communal obligation (fard kifayah) that is not bound by the same temporal limitations as individual voluntary or obligatory prayers. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the time for funeral prayer is flexible, provided it is performed before the body is buried.
